tagline.text: An old 1909 water-supply dam in a gorge between two mountains, now a swimming spot

location.label: Location
location.text: Wawa Gorge, Barangay San Rafael, Rodriguez, Rizal

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (more water and murkier in the rainy season)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱200–700 (transport, environmental entrance fee and snacks, plus a raft or cottage if you choose, per person)

children.text: Wawa Dam is an old water-supply dam that began operating in 1909 in the gorge between Mount Pamitinan and Mount Binacayan. Today it is used for bamboo rafts, swimming and as a trailhead for hikes, and at about an hour from Manila it makes a good day trip.

Wawa Dam is a gravity dam in Wawa Gorge, Rodriguez (formerly Montalban), Rizal. It was built across the Marikina River between Mount Pamitinan and Mount Binacayan, which face each other, and the name Wawa is said to mean "entrance" in the Dumagat language. It lies at the western edge of the Sierra Madre range, about an hour from central Manila. Today it is used for recreation rather than water supply, and the dam and its surroundings are part of the Pamitinan Protected Landscape.

Construction began in 1904 under American colonial rule, the dam went into service in 1909, and its original purpose was to supply water to Manila. It is listed as about 85 meters (280 feet) long with a maximum water depth of about 13 meters, and described as a slightly arched gravity dam. After Angat Dam was completed in the 1960s, it stopped serving as a water source around 1968 and became known as a scenic abandoned dam. Near the end of World War II, US and Japanese forces fought in the hills around here, recorded as the Battle of Wawa Dam. In 2019 the National Museum is said to have recognized the site as an Important Cultural Property. The fighting ran from March to May 1945 between the US Army's XI Corps and the Imperial Japanese Army's Shimbu Group in the Montalban and Antipolo hills, and the dam area was a key position. The operator is listed as the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS), and the reservoir's normal elevation is given as about 57 meters. There is also an account that public pressure to reuse the dam grew when Manila faced water shortages.

For travelers, Wawa Dam has three faces. The first is as a hiking trailhead. Climbs of Mount Pamitinan and Mount Binacayan begin from this village. The second is as a swimming spot, where you can swim below the dam and among the rocks around it and rent a cottage to rest. The third is the scenery. Limestone cliffs rising on both sides of the gorge and bamboo rafts on the calm reservoir fit into one view. One guide, citing local government figures, says nearly two thousand visitors a week come on weekends.

This guide is for travelers looking for a creek swimming spot near Manila and a scenic old dam. It resembles a summer valley outing in Korea, but in the Philippines you should pay more attention to hygiene, safety and local guide rules. The fees and rules here come mostly from 2024–2025 visitor accounts and are not officially confirmed. Check the latest information with the Rodriguez tourism office or other official channels before you go.

blocks.title: The old dam and gorge scenery

children.text: A low concrete dam stretches across the gorge, with a mountain rising on each side. The best photos come from looking toward the gorge from the dam or its edge. The length is listed as about

. In places there are no safety railings at the dam structure and edges, so do not stand at the very end. In the morning the cliffs on both sides cast cool shade, while at midday sunlight reflects off the limestone and glares, so bring a hat and sunglasses. When taking photos on the rocks, be careful because moss can make the ground slippery.

Bamboo rafting on the calm water above the dam is well known. There is a pleasure in floating slowly between two mountains and looking up at the gorge. Check prices and whether it is operating locally. Ask first whether life jackets are provided.
Many people swim among the rocks and shallow water below the dam. Avoid places with strong currents, and always stay close to children. After rain the water is muddy and rising, so do not go in.
Bamboo cottages stand around the dam, and 2022–2025 visitor reports put them (peak season) at
₱200 and up

. Stalls sell fruit, drinks and snacks, so you can grab a bite. Some reviews say there is a small charge each time you use the toilet. On weekends the cottages fill up early in the morning, so go on a weekday or arrive early to claim a spot.

The paths to Mount Pamitinan and Mount Binacayan begin in Wawa village. It is common to see hikers cooling off at the dam after coming down. Climbing requires separate registration and a guide, so read the Mount Pamitinan article too. Registration is described as taking place at the DENR registration desk and the tourism office in Wawa village, but rules change from year to year, so check as soon as you arrive.

A legend tells of the giant Bernardo Carpio trapped between the two mountains, and another story says earthquakes are him pushing the rocks apart. Ask a local guide and you can hear more of the story.

Upstream, the Wawa Pumped Storage project is said to be under way. It plans an artificial lake of about 400 hectares to run a 600-megawatt-class energy storage facility, and reports say impounding began in July 2024. How this project will affect visits to Wawa Dam should be checked in local announcements.
Take a UV Express van from Cubao in Manila to Rodriguez.
From Rodriguez, take a tricycle to the entrance of Wawa village, pay the environmental fee and go in.

Return to the village, buy souvenirs and snacks, and leave for Manila.
On weekends the cottages fill up first, so arrive early in the morning. The environmental fee and parking are often paid together at the entrance, so keep the receipt or ticket.

children.text: The walk from the entrance to the dam follows a ridge path and is described as taking about
5–20 minutes
. The short distance is listed at about
Shoes with good grip are better than sandals.
Wawa Dam is known as a route for beginner to intermediate cyclists, and it is mostly paved. Check bicycle rental and road conditions locally.
Swimming and walking are easier in the dry season. In the rainy season the reservoir rises, the water is murky and the stream flows fast, so it may not be suitable for swimming.
March to May is hot, and swimming crowds are largest. Weekday mornings are quiet, while on weekends and holidays cottages and parking fill early.

In strong sun from March to May, arrive in the morning, enjoy rafting and a walk first, and rest in the shade of a cottage at midday. You need to catch a van back to Manila before dark, so get ready to leave before 3 p.m. In the rainy season showers can come suddenly, so check the weather forecast before planning.

There is almost nowhere to stay in Wawa village or around the dam, so most people make a day trip from Manila. If you need a bed, look for small lodgings in Rodriguez or Montalban and check recent reviews on booking sites. Camping in the village is subject to rules, so check locally.

For food, stalls around the dam sell fruit, drinks and simple snacks. Many visitors rent a cottage and eat packed meals brought from Manila, and you must carry out your trash. There are small eateries at the village entrance, but the choice is limited, so bring plenty of water and snacks.

Many visitors bring a mat and a cooler as they would for a Korean valley outing, but check locally for cottage rules and whether outside food is allowed. After swimming it helps to have a change of clothes and a plastic bag, and avoid sitting in the van home in wet clothes. Stalls at the village entrance mostly take cash only.
Bring plenty of small change. The environmental fee, parking and toilets are paid in cash.
Weekday mornings are quiet and it is easier to find a cottage.
Bring swimwear, a change of clothes, a towel and a waterproof bag.
Wear shoes with good grip and avoid sandals.
Ask for a life jacket when riding a bamboo raft.
If you plan to hike, ask in Wawa village about registration and a guide first.
Carry out your trash and do not leave it at the dam or in the gorge.
Put belongings in a waterproof bag and do not leave valuables in the cottage.
Ask local guides or vendors for the price first, and check whether it is negotiable before you use a service.
After rain, the current in the reservoir and discharge areas suddenly becomes strong and deep. Do not go into the water if it is raining or has just stopped.
The edge of the dam and the gorge rocks are slippery and in places have no railings, so there is a risk of falling.
Depth varies by area and warning signs may be few, so weak swimmers and children should wear life jackets and play only in shallow water.
On weekends cottages and parking fill in an instant, so arrive early.
It is described as having been closed for a time in 2023 and reopened, so check whether it is open before you go.
Access rules may change because of upstream development and other projects, so check the latest announcements.
Direct sun is strong at midday, so you need a hat, sunscreen and plenty of water.
